pr_title: Invalidate ExecCtx now before computing timeouts in all repeating timer events using a WorkSerializer or combiner
pr_body:
This is a tactical alternative to https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/26064

Related: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/26079

I'd still like to find a structural change to fix https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/26079 without needing to pay close attention to whether or not that kind of issue can affect a certain code path, but this change should fix the user issue mentioned in b/185205431 in the meantime.
pr_comments:
The code changes LGTM, modulo the chttp2 change, which @yashykt should review.

Can you please add a comment above the `InvalidateNow()` calls you're adding to indicate why they're needed?  Otherwise, future readers may remove them, not understanding why they're needed.

Also, is there a way to add tests for these specific cases?  I don't want to block this fix on that if the tests are too hard to write, but if they aren't too hard, it seems better to have them.
I'll review in a bit. I haven't read through the issue yet.

I agree it would be great to get a unit test for this, but it indeed appears difficult to write such a test, and a benchmark style test like the one mentioned in https://buganizer.corp.google.com/issues/185205431#comment15 is IMO the most effective way to test for this, since the failure mode manifests itself with some operations taking much longer than they should (but they can still complete). Also, the problem seems to repro so far only on single-core VMs (which we can be easily controlled for in an e2e benchmark style test).

(after this PR is imported, I plan to run the repro from https://buganizer.corp.google.com/issues/185205431#comment15 continuously).

issue_context.title: Time caching in ExecCtx can cause indefinite busy loops due to time skew between threads
comments: Reopening since #26086 is more a workaround for this problem (didn't mean to close this). A more general fix is probably needed here, since the current situation is still error prone as mentioned.

I believe this is going to be fixed via the promise conversion.  As part of that, we will do time caching for each call individually within the promise, and we will not do any caching for control plane operations or timers.  The time cache within `ExecCtx` will go away completely.
It's still a problem until we finish the migration to promises.

review_comments: I'm not sure about this one -- @yashykt should review this one.
This does run within a combiner if that's what the original question is

The more I think about this, the more I'm thinking that we should either not cache `Now()` at all or maybe we should add `InvalidateNow()` at some more general locations, for example, when closures are executed on the work serializer/combiner
